# x86_64 ONLY, and this is a wheel-availability fact rather than a preference:
# unicodedata2 publishes no cp311 aarch64 wheel at ANY version (checked 17.0.0
# and the five releases before it -- cp310 and cp312 aarch64 exist, cp311 does
# not), and `--only-binary=:all:` forbids building the sdist.
#
# Excluding it on ARM is safe because NO hosted entrypoint imports it. Its only
# importer is scripts/baseline_places_construction_v1.py, the independent Python
# re-implementation used for semantic-digest parity in tests -- it is absent from
# check_hosted_imports' module set and is never invoked by construction-v1.yml.
# The production transform is Rust, which carries its own Unicode 17.0 tables and
# const-asserts the version. CI's Python Pipeline runs on x86_64 and still gets
# the package, so the parity tests keep running.
unicodedata2==17.0.0 ; platform_machine == "x86_64" \
    --hash=sha256:50036b14ac5c53b607b0b98c67e0dfab5b1029e03735a7c2a0db6e563e0b0375 \
    --hash=sha256:95443d08ef6e6daf8d749f187d16c6ed90ab8bb47ad6f2fb616517fad0e6d5bf
# The S3/R2 client construction-v1 publishes and hydrates through
# (scripts/r2_verified_store.py Boto3Store). It is here rather than left to the
# `aws` CLI because `aws` v2 costs 0.339 s of CPU per invocation before it does
# any work -- measured, ten runs of `aws --version`: wall 3.39 s, user 3.11 s +
# sys 0.28 s. Finalize makes two calls per published object, so a planet address
# slice at 65,751 objects is 131,502 invocations = 12.4 hours serial and still
# ~3.1 hours at a 4-vCPU ceiling, against a 360-minute job timeout. That was the
# top blocker for a planet dispatch.
#
# Every wheel below is `py3-none-any`, so these hashes are platform- and
# interpreter-independent -- unlike numpy's above, which is why a local venv on
# 3.12 has to skip --require-hashes while hosted runners on 3.11.14 do not.
